name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28H disrupts the IP6-dependent PH-TH dimer interface of BTK. The His side chain at position 28 cannot make the contacts the arginine makes across the dimer, so the dimer does not form and BTK activation at the membrane is impaired.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E9", "E11", "E5", "E7"], "would_refute": "A model of the PH-TH dimer (built from the IP6-bound PH domain structures, for example by superposing 1B55 on the E41K dimer) shows residue 28 with no atom within about 5 \u00c5 of the partner protomer in any predicted dimer pose, and the R28H change does not alter the interface contact count or buried surface area.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "E9 is the only record item that states a mechanism for this exact substitution (R28H impairs PH-TH dimerization), so it carries the most weight. E11 supports the dimer but is about E41K, not R28H. The dimer interface itself is unresolved: G3 says no structure shows how position 28 maps onto it, and no dimer structure is in the record. Still missing: a dimer model or an experiment that measures dimerization for R28H."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "The R28 side chain is part of the inositol-phosphate headgroup pocket of the BTK PH domain. Replacing arginine with histidine removes the positive charge and the geometry needed to coordinate the phosphate groups of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or IP6, which reduces ligand affinity and membrane recruitment.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E6", "E17", "E13", "E15"], "would_refute": "In ligand-bound PH-domain structures (1B55 with IP4, and any other inositol-phosphate-bound entry), residue 28 has no atom within about 4 \u00c5 of any ligand phosphate oxygen, and an R28H model docked or superposed with IP4 shows the same ligand contacts and binding energy as the wild type within the MM/PBSA uncertainty.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Residue 28 is annotated as an inositol-phosphate binding site (E6) and sits in the IP4 complex 1B55 (E17). E13 reports that R28H changes Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 binding in MD, which is variant-specific. This is still computational only (E13, E15), and the record contains no measured binding for R28H (G1). Ligand binding and dimerisation are coupled (E11), so this may be the upstream cause of H1 rather than a separate route. Still missing: a binding measurement or a ligand-bound structure of R28H."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28H destabilises the PH domain fold. The residue lies in the beta strand (residues 25-32) and its arginine side chain makes intra-domain packing or salt-bridge contacts that the histidine cannot keep, which lowers folding stability and reduces the amount of soluble, folded protein.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E7", "E10", "E12", "E18"], "would_refute": "Predicted \u0394\u0394G for R28H from folding-stability tools (run on the AlphaFold DB model AF-Q06187-F1 and on 1B55 and 6TT2) is below about 1 kcal/mol, and residue 28 is solvent-exposed with no buried intra-domain partner in the crystal structures or in the AlphaFold model, so the side chain makes no packing contact to remove.", "starting_rank": 3, "rank_rationale": "The support is indirect: a beta-strand annotation (E7), high conservation (E10, 0.962), a damaging popEVE score (E12), and a confident AlphaFold model (E18, pLDDT 84). Still missing: a \u0394\u0394G or expression measurement for R28H."}
